blurb.en: An if does not need True or False. Any value can be tested, and a short rule decides which values count as false.
blurb.zh: if 不一定要 True 或 False。任何值都能拿来判断，一条很短的规矩决定哪些值算假。

en: An if does not need a True or False. Give it any value and Python asks that value whether it counts as true. The rule is short: zero in any number type, the empty string, empty containers ([], {}, ()), None and False are falsy. Everything else is truthy.

The surprises are all about being non-empty. "0" is a string holding one character, not the number 0, so it is truthy. " " holds a space, so it is not empty and it is truthy. Even "False" is truthy, because the only falsy string is the empty one. [0] and [[]] are truthy too: a list with something in it is non-empty, whatever that something is.

That is why show_items hands the list itself to the if. Asking whether its length is above zero gets the same answer with more words; testing the value directly is the usual Python style, and it works unchanged for strings, dictionaries and tuples.

bool() converts any value to True or False by exactly the same rule, which is useful when you want to see the answer printed, as the line of three bool() calls does. Inside an if you do not need it: the if already makes that conversion.
zh: if 不一定要 True 或 False。交给它任何值，Python 都会去问这个值算不算真。规矩很短：各种数字类型里的零、空字符串、空容器（[]、{}、()）、None 和 False 是假值，其余的都是真值。
出人意料的地方都跟「非空」有关。"0" 是一个装着一个字符的字符串，不是数字 0，所以是真值。" " 里有一个空格，不是空串，所以也是真值。连 "False" 都是真值——唯一的假字符串是空串。[0] 和 [[]] 也是真值：列表里只要有东西就不是空的，不管那东西是什么。
所以 show_items 直接把列表本身交给 if。去问它的长度是否大于零，得到的是同一个答案、只是多写几个字；直接判断这个值是 Python 通常的写法，而且对字符串、字典、元组都原样适用。
bool() 按同一条规矩把任何值变成 True 或 False，想把答案打印出来看时很有用，比如那行连着三个 bool() 调用。在 if 里用不着它：if 自己已经做了这次转换。

lineNotes.en: repr() in the loop body shows strings with their quotes, so the empty string, "0" and a single space can be told apart in the output.
lineNotes.zh: 循环体里的 repr() 会把字符串连引号一起显示，输出里才分得清空串、"0" 和一个空格。

lineNotes.en: True, True, False: a non-empty string, a list holding one (empty) list, and an empty tuple.
lineNotes.zh: True、True、False：一个非空字符串、一个装着一个（空）列表的列表、一个空元组。

title.en: Short-Circuit and / or, and the Conditional Expression
title.zh: 短路的 and / or 与条件表达式

blurb.en: and and or hand back one of their operands and stop as soon as the answer is known - which makes them defaults and guards. Plus choosing a value in one line.
blurb.zh: and 与 or 交回的是某一个操作数，而且答案一定下来就停——于是它们能当默认值、当守卫。外加在一行里二选一。

en: and and or do not have to give back True or False. or gives back its left operand if that is truthy, and its right operand otherwise. and gives back its left operand if that is falsy, and its right operand otherwise. So 0 or [] or "last" works along the chain to the first truthy value, and 3 and "x" and 0 works along to the first falsy one - or to the last value, if every one is truthy.

That makes or a neat way to supply a default: an empty nickname is falsy, so the full name comes back instead. The catch is that every falsy value triggers the default, so use it only when every falsy value really does mean missing - a score of 0 is a real score, and or would throw it away.

Both operators short-circuit: they stop as soon as the answer is known. The loud() lines prove it. With and, a falsy left side already decides the answer, so loud(1) is never called and checked is printed only once; with or, a truthy left side decides it, so loud(3) is never called. That is what makes and a guard: in is_high_average the division on the right is never attempted when count is 0, so there is no ZeroDivisionError. first_letter uses the same idea to avoid indexing an empty string.

A conditional expression - a value, then if and a condition, then else and another value - chooses between two values inside one expression, so it can go straight after return. It reads well for a short choice like the one in parity; once either side needs more than a value, an ordinary if statement is clearer.
zh: and 和 or 交回的不一定是 True 或 False。or 在左操作数为真时交回左操作数，否则交回右操作数。and 在左操作数为假时交回左操作数，否则交回右操作数。所以 0 or [] or "last" 沿着链一路找到第一个真值，3 and "x" and 0 一路找到第一个假值——要是全都为真，就交回最后一个。
这让 or 成了提供默认值的顺手办法：空昵称是假值，于是交回全名。问题在于任何假值都会触发默认值，所以只有当每一种假值真的都表示「没有」时才用它——0 分是一个真实的分数，or 会把它扔掉。

两个运算符都会短路：答案一定下来就停。loud() 那两行就是证据。and 的左边为假时答案已经定了，所以 loud(1) 根本没被调用，checked 只打印一次；or 的左边为真时答案也定了，所以 loud(3) 没被调用。正是这一点让 and 能当守卫：is_high_average 里 count 为 0 时，右边的除法根本不会去算，也就没有 ZeroDivisionError。first_letter 用同一个思路，避免去取空串的下标。
条件表达式——一个值，接 if 和条件，再接 else 和另一个值——在一个表达式里二选一，所以能直接写在 return 后面。像 parity 里这样简短的选择读起来很顺；两边一旦不只是一个值，普通的 if 语句更清楚。

lineNotes.en: When count is 0 the left side is False, and and hands back False without ever doing the division.
lineNotes.zh: count 为 0 时左边是 False，and 直接交回 False，除法一次也不做。

lineNotes.en: Output: one checked line, then 0. loud(0) returned a falsy value, so loud(1) never ran.
lineNotes.zh: 输出：一行 checked，然后是 0。loud(0) 交回的是假值，所以 loud(1) 从没运行。

lineNotes.en: Prints last and 0: or stops at the first truthy value, and stops at the first falsy one.
lineNotes.zh: 打印 last 和 0：or 停在第一个真值上，and 停在第一个假值上。

title.en: Grade Boundaries: elif from the Top Down
title.zh: 成绩等级：elif 从高往低

blurb.en: Each test names only a lower bound, which works because an elif chain stops at the first true condition - so the order of the lines is part of the logic.
blurb.zh: 每个判断只写下界。这之所以行得通，是因为 elif 链停在第一个为真的条件上——所以行的先后顺序本身就是逻辑的一部分。

en: An elif chain is tested from the top, and the first condition that is true wins; every branch below it is skipped. That is what lets each test name only a lower bound. By the time the chain asks whether mark >= 60, it already knows the mark is below 70 - otherwise an earlier branch would have caught it.

So the program is only correct because of the order its lines are in. Move the C test above the A test and a mark of 95 gets a C: it is at least 60, and nothing ever asks the A question. Nothing warns you - the program still runs, it is just wrong.
It also depends on elif. With a separate if on every line, a mark of 95 would pass all four tests one after another, and letter would end up as "D", because the last assignment wins.
The boundaries are 80, 70, 60 and 50 for a mark out of 100. Compare with grade-boundaries-ranges, which writes every range in full so that the order stops mattering. Both print the same ten lines.
zh: elif 链从上往下判断，第一个为真的条件胜出，它下面的分支全部跳过。正因为这样，每个判断才可以只写下界。链走到问 mark >= 60 的时候，已经知道分数低于 70——否则前面的分支早就把它接走了。
所以这个程序之所以正确，全靠行的先后顺序。把判 C 的那条挪到判 A 的上面，95 分就会得 C：它确实至少 60 分，而判 A 的问题永远轮不到。不会有任何警告——程序照样运行，只是错了。
它也依赖 elif。要是每一行都各写一个 if，95 分会一个接一个地通过全部四个判断，letter 最后变成 "D"，因为最后一次赋值说了算。
等级界线是满分 100 的 80、70、60、50。和 grade-boundaries-ranges 对照着看：那个版本把每个区间都写全，于是顺序不再要紧。两个程序打印的十行完全相同。

lineNotes.en: Everything below 50 lands here. else needs no condition: every other case has already been ruled out.
lineNotes.zh: 低于 50 的都落到这里。else 不需要条件：其他情况都已经被排除了。

lineNotes.en: One return at the end, after the chain has picked exactly one assignment.
lineNotes.zh: 末尾只有一个 return，这时链已经恰好挑中了一次赋值。

blurb.en: Each branch spells out its whole range with a chained comparison, so no branch depends on the ones above it - and the order stops mattering.
blurb.zh: 每个分支都用链式比较写全自己的区间，于是没有哪个分支依赖它上面的分支——顺序也就不再要紧。

en: A chained comparison such as 60 <= mark < 70 means 60 <= mark and mark < 70, with mark written only once. It reads the way the range is written in maths.

Because the ranges do not overlap, at most one of them can be true for any mark, so the branches could be written in any order and the result would be the same. That is the trade against grade-boundaries-descending: more to write on each line, but no line depends on the lines above it.

Lower bound with <=, upper bound with a strict <: that way every boundary mark belongs to exactly one range. 70 is in B's range and not in C's. Write <= at both ends and 70 would be inside two ranges, so the order would start to matter again; write < at both ends and 70 would be inside none and fall through to U.

The A range has an upper bound of 100, so a mark above 100 falls through to U here, while grade-boundaries-descending would call it an A. For every real mark from 0 to 100 the two agree, and both print the same ten lines.
zh: 像 60 <= mark < 70 这样的链式比较，意思是 60 <= mark and mark < 70，mark 只写一次。读起来和数学里写区间一样。
区间互不重叠，任何分数至多落进其中一个，所以分支按什么顺序写，结果都一样。这就是它和 grade-boundaries-descending 的取舍：每行多写一点，但没有哪一行依赖它上面的行。
下界用 <=，上界用严格的 <：这样每个界线上的分数都恰好属于一个区间。70 在 B 的区间里，不在 C 的区间里。两头都写 <=，70 就同时在两个区间里，顺序又变得要紧了；两头都写 <，70 哪个区间都不在，一路落到 U。
A 的区间有上界 100，所以超过 100 的分数在这里落到 U，而 grade-boundaries-descending 会给它 A。对 0 到 100 之间真实的分数，两个版本结论一致，打印的十行也完全相同。

lineNotes.en: The top range includes both of its ends: 100 is a possible mark, and there is no grade above A for it to belong to.
lineNotes.zh: 最高的区间两头都包含：100 是可能的分数，而且 A 之上没有别的等级可以接住它。

lineNotes.en: Read it as: at least 60 and below 70. The < at the top end hands 70 to the B range instead.
lineNotes.zh: 读作：至少 60 且低于 70。上端的 < 把 70 让给了 B 的区间。

blurb.en: The leap-year rule written the way it is said - one condition inside another, three levels deep.
blurb.zh: 闰年规则照着说法写下来——一个条件套在另一个里面，套三层。

en: The rule has three parts. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year - except a whole century (a year divisible by 100), which is a leap year only if it is also divisible by 400. So 2024 is a leap year and 2023 is not; 1900 and 2100 are not, but 2000 and 2400 are.

The nested version follows those words one level at a time. The outer if asks about 4; only inside it does the question about 100 make sense; only inside that does 400 matter. Every if has its own else, so you can point at any return and say exactly which answers led to it.
A remainder of 0 is how divisible is written: year % 4 == 0 asks whether dividing by 4 leaves nothing over.

The cost is width and repetition: three levels of indentation, four returns, and True and False written out by hand. Compare with leap-year-one-expression, where the same rule becomes a single line. Both share days_in_february and print the same six lines.
zh: 规则分三层。能被 4 整除的年份是闰年——但整百年（能被 100 整除的年份）例外，它还得能被 400 整除才是闰年。所以 2024 是闰年，2023 不是；1900 和 2100 不是，2000 和 2400 是。
嵌套版本一层一层地跟着这段话走。外层 if 问 4；只有进到它里面，问 100 才有意义；只有再进一层，400 才要紧。每个 if 都有自己的 else，所以随便指着哪个 return，都说得出是哪几个回答把程序带到了那里。
「整除」写成余数为 0：year % 4 == 0 问的是除以 4 之后是不是什么都不剩。
代价是宽度和重复：缩进三层、四个 return、True 和 False 都得手写出来。和 leap-year-one-expression 对照着看，同一条规则在那里只有一行。两个程序共用 days_in_february，打印的六行完全相同。

lineNotes.en: This else belongs to the century test: divisible by 4 and not a whole century, so a leap year.
lineNotes.zh: 这个 else 属于判整百年的那个 if：能被 4 整除、又不是整百年，所以是闰年。

lineNotes.en: One year for each path through the nesting, including both kinds of century.
lineNotes.zh: 嵌套里的每条路径各配一个年份，两种整百年都有。

blurb.en: The same leap-year rule as a single boolean expression: a comparison already is True or False, so the function can return it directly.
blurb.zh: 同一条闰年规则写成一个布尔表达式：比较本身就是 True 或 False，所以函数可以直接把它交回去。

en: The rule has three parts. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year - except a whole century (a year divisible by 100), which is a leap year only if it is also divisible by 400. So 2024 is a leap year and 2023 is not; 1900 and 2100 are not, but 2000 and 2400 are.

A comparison already is True or False, so a function that would only ever return True or False can usually return the expression itself, with no if at all. and needs both of its sides to be true; or needs at least one.

The brackets say what the rule says. Without them Python would group it as (divisible by 4 and not a century) or divisible by 400, because and is worked out before or. That happens to give the same answers - every year divisible by 400 is divisible by 4 as well - but it no longer reads like the rule, and the next person to change it has to work that out. Keep the brackets.

Short-circuiting keeps it cheap: for three years out of four the first test is already False, and the part in brackets is never looked at. Compare with leap-year-nested: same rule, same days_in_february, same six lines of output.
zh: 规则分三层。能被 4 整除的年份是闰年——但整百年（能被 100 整除的年份）例外，它还得能被 400 整除才是闰年。所以 2024 是闰年，2023 不是；1900 和 2100 不是，2000 和 2400 是。
比较本身就是 True 或 False，所以一个只会交回 True 或 False 的函数，通常可以直接交回这个表达式，一个 if 都不用。and 要求两边都为真；or 只要至少一边为真。
括号表达的正是规则本身。没有括号，Python 会把它分组成（能被 4 整除 and 不是整百年）or 能被 400 整除，因为 and 比 or 先算。碰巧答案一样——能被 400 整除的年份一定也能被 4 整除——但它读起来不再像那条规则，下一个来改它的人还得先把这一点想明白。括号留着。
短路让它很省事：四个年份里有三个，第一个判断就已经是 False，括号里那部分根本不看。和 leap-year-nested 对照着看：同一条规则、同一个 days_in_february、同样的六行输出。

lineNotes.en: Written exactly as in leap-year-nested, so the two programs differ only in is_leap.
lineNotes.zh: 与 leap-year-nested 里的一字不差，所以两个程序只在 is_leap 上不同。

lineNotes.en: The same six years as the nested version: one ordinary leap year, one ordinary year, two centuries that are not leap years and two that are.
lineNotes.zh: 和嵌套版本同样的六个年份：一个普通闰年、一个普通平年、两个不是闰年的整百年、两个是闰年的整百年。

blurb.en: Split the visitors into groups, then split each group again - every question asked only of the people it applies to.
blurb.zh: 先把游客分成两组，再把每组继续分下去——每个问题只问给它适用的那些人。

en: The prices: under 5 is free; 5 to 17 pays 5; 65 and over pays 6; every other adult pays 8 with a student card and 12 without one. Being a student only changes the price for adults under 65.

The nested version splits the visitors in two first - under 18 or not - and then splits each half again. Each question is only asked of the people it applies to: whether someone is a student is only asked once they are known to be an adult under 65.
Every path ends in its own return, so you can trace any visitor by answering the questions from the top: 12 and a student is under 18, not under 5, and pays 5 - the student card never comes into it.

The shape is its weakness. Every new rule adds another level and pushes the real work further to the right, and an else near the bottom is a long way from the if it belongs to. Compare with ticket-price-guard-clauses: the same rules, the same eight lines of output, and no nesting.
zh: 票价规则：不到 5 岁免费；5 到 17 岁付 5；65 岁及以上付 6；其余成年人有学生证付 8，没有付 12。是不是学生，只对 65 岁以下的成年人有影响。
嵌套版本先把游客一分为二——是否未满 18——再把每一半继续分下去。每个问题只问给它适用的人：是不是学生，只有在确定对方是 65 岁以下的成年人之后才问。
每条路径都以自己的 return 结束，所以任何一位游客，都可以从上往下回答问题来追踪：12 岁的学生未满 18、不是不到 5 岁，付 5——学生证根本用不上。
它的形状就是它的弱点。每多一条规则就多一层，真正干活的代码被推得越来越靠右；靠近底部的 else 离它所属的 if 隔得很远。和 ticket-price-guard-clauses 对照着看：同样的规则、同样的八行输出，没有嵌套。

lineNotes.en: The first split: children on one side, adults on the other.
lineNotes.zh: 第一刀：孩子一边，成年人一边。

lineNotes.en: Four levels of indentation: an adult, under 65, and not a student.
lineNotes.zh: 缩进四层：成年人、不到 65 岁、不是学生。

blurb.en: Deal with one case at a time and return at once: every later line may assume the earlier cases did not apply, and the code stays flat.
blurb.zh: 一次处理一种情况、当场 return：后面的每一行都可以认定前面的情况不成立，代码始终是平的。

en: The prices: under 5 is free; 5 to 17 pays 5; 65 and over pays 6; every other adult pays 8 with a student card and 12 without one. Being a student only changes the price for adults under 65.

A guard clause deals with one case and returns straight away. Once a return has run, nothing below it in the function runs, so every later line may assume that none of the earlier cases applied: by the time the student test is reached, the visitor is known to be from 18 to 64.
That is also why no elif and no else are needed - a return already leaves the function. The last line has no if at all: anyone who reaches it is an adult, under 65, and not a student.

The order of the guards still matters, as in any chain of early returns: put the under-18 test above the under-5 test and a three-year-old would pay 5. But the code stays flat, and a new rule is one more pair of lines rather than one more level. Compare with ticket-price-nested.
zh: 票价规则：不到 5 岁免费；5 到 17 岁付 5；65 岁及以上付 6；其余成年人有学生证付 8，没有付 12。是不是学生，只对 65 岁以下的成年人有影响。
守卫子句处理一种情况，然后立刻 return。return 一旦执行，函数里它下面的代码就都不会再执行，所以后面的每一行都可以认定前面的情况都不成立：走到判断学生的那一行时，已经知道游客在 18 到 64 岁之间。
这也是不需要 elif、也不需要 else 的原因——return 已经离开了函数。最后一行连 if 都没有：能走到那里的，一定是成年人、不到 65 岁、不是学生。
守卫之间的顺序仍然要紧，任何一串提前 return 都是如此：把判未满 18 的挪到判不到 5 岁的上面，三岁的孩子就要付 5。但代码是平的，多一条规则只是多两行，而不是多一层。和 ticket-price-nested 对照着看。

lineNotes.en: The first guard. Its return means no line below this one ever sees a visitor under 5.
lineNotes.zh: 第一道守卫。它的 return 意味着下面没有任何一行会再遇到不到 5 岁的游客。

lineNotes.en: No condition needed: every other case has already returned.
lineNotes.zh: 不需要条件：其他情况全都已经 return 了。

blurb.en: Nine possible pairs of moves, decided by one subtraction and one remainder instead of nine separate cases.
blurb.zh: 九种出招组合，用一次减法加一次取余来判，而不是写九种情况。

en: Written out case by case, rock-paper-scissors needs nine answers. Numbering the moves turns it into arithmetic: rock is 0, paper is 1, scissors is 2, and each move beats the one just before it in the list - paper beats rock, scissors beats paper - with rock beating scissors by wrapping round from the start of the list to the end.

So subtract the two positions and take the remainder mod 3. The same move gives 0, a draw. When the first move is one place after the second the result is 1; when that place is reached by wrapping round (rock minus scissors is 0 - 2, which is -2) the remainder still comes out as 1. The only other possible result is 2, which means the second move is one place after the first: player 2 wins.

Python's % always gives a result with the same sign as the number after it, so a remainder mod 3 is always 0, 1 or 2 - the last line of output shows -2 % 3 and -1 % 3. Many other languages (C, Java, JavaScript) give a negative remainder there, which is why code written for them often adds 3 before taking the remainder.
MOVES.index finds a move's position in the list. The function trusts both moves to be spelled exactly as in MOVES; anything else raises a ValueError.
zh: 逐种情况写出来，石头剪刀布要九个答案。给出招编号就把它变成了算术：石头 0、布 1、剪刀 2，每一招都赢列表里紧挨在它前面的那一招——布赢石头、剪刀赢布——而石头赢剪刀，是从列表开头绕回到末尾。
所以把两个位置相减，再对 3 取余。出同一招得 0，平局。第一招正好在第二招后面一位时得 1；这一位若是绕回去才到的（石头减剪刀是 0 - 2，等于 -2），余数照样是 1。剩下唯一可能的结果是 2，意思是第二招在第一招后面一位：玩家 2 赢。
Python 的 % 得到的结果总是和 % 后面那个数同号，所以对 3 取余永远是 0、1 或 2——输出最后一行显示的就是 -2 % 3 和 -1 % 3。很多别的语言（C、Java、JavaScript）在这里会得到负的余数，所以为它们写的代码常常在取余之前先加 3。
MOVES.index 找出一招在列表里的位置。函数默认两招都和 MOVES 里拼写一致；拼错了会抛 ValueError。

lineNotes.en: The order is the whole trick: each move beats the one listed just before it, and rock beats the last one.
lineNotes.zh: 整个诀窍就在这个顺序里：每一招都赢排在它前面的那一招，石头赢最后那一招。

lineNotes.en: Prints 1 2. In Python the remainder takes the sign of the divisor, 3.
lineNotes.zh: 打印 1 2。Python 里余数的符号跟随除数 3。

run.expect:
rock v rock -> draw
rock v paper -> player 2
rock v scissors -> player 1
paper v rock -> player 1
paper v paper -> draw
paper v scissors -> player 2
scissors v rock -> player 2
scissors v paper -> player 1
scissors v scissors -> draw
1 2

blurb.en: One guard clause rejects every set of lengths that cannot make a triangle; after it, the tests for equilateral, isosceles and scalene can be simple.
blurb.zh: 一个守卫子句挡掉所有构不成三角形的边长；过了它，判等边、等腰、不等边就都可以写得很简单。

en: Three lengths make a triangle only if every pair of sides adds up to more than the third side - the triangle inequality. The guard clause tests the opposite: if any pair adds up to no more than the third side, the answer is not a triangle, and the function returns before the other tests run.

No more than, not less than. 1, 2, 3 has 1 + 2 exactly equal to 3, so its three corners lie on one straight line - a flat shape, not a triangle. The same test also rejects zero and negative lengths with no extra check: if a is 0 or less, a + b is at most b and a + c is at most c, so one of the first two cases must hold. The last two rows of output (0, 4, 4 and -1, 5, 5) show it.

After the guard, the other tests may assume a real triangle. == can be chained just like <, and a chain of equalities is true only when every value in it is equal. Isosceles means at least two equal sides, so that test has to come after the equilateral one - an equilateral triangle would pass it too.
5, 5, 8 and 5, 8, 5 are the same triangle with its sides listed in a different order, which is why the isosceles test compares all three pairs rather than just a and b.
zh: 三个长度要构成三角形，必须任意两边之和都大于第三边——这就是三角不等式。守卫子句判的是反面：只要有一对边之和不大于第三边，答案就是「不是三角形」，函数在其他判断之前就 return。
是「不大于」，不是「小于」。1、2、3 里 1 + 2 恰好等于 3，三个顶点落在一条直线上——是扁平的一条线，不是三角形。这同一个判断还顺带挡掉了零和负数长度，不用另外检查：a 小于等于 0 时，a + b 至多是 b，a + c 至多是 c，所以前两种情况里必有一种成立。输出最后两行（0, 4, 4 和 -1, 5, 5）就是证明。
过了守卫，后面的判断就可以认定这是一个真三角形。== 能像 < 一样连着写，一串相等比较只有在其中每个值都相等时才为真。等腰是至少两边相等，所以这个判断必须放在判等边之后——等边三角形也会通过它。
5, 5, 8 和 5, 8, 5 是同一个三角形，只是边的列出顺序不同——所以判等腰要比较全部三对，而不只是 a 和 b。

lineNotes.at: if a == b or b == c or a == c:
lineNotes.en: Any one equal pair is enough. The equilateral case never gets here: it has already returned.
lineNotes.zh: 有一对相等就够了。等边的情况到不了这里：它已经 return 了。

lineNotes.en: Reached only by a real triangle with no two sides equal.
lineNotes.zh: 只有没有任何两边相等的真三角形才会走到这里。

run.expect:
3 3 3 equilateral
5 5 8 isosceles
5 8 5 isosceles
3 4 5 scalene
1 2 3 not a triangle
2 9 4 not a triangle
0 4 4 not a triangle
-1 5 5 not a triangle

blurb.en: Check both of De Morgan's laws the brute-force way: try every combination of two inputs and compare the two sides.
blurb.zh: 用最笨也最可靠的办法验证德摩根的两条定律：两个输入的每种组合都试一遍，比较两边。

en: De Morgan's laws say what happens when not is applied to a bracket. In the symbols exam papers use, ¬(A ∧ B) is the same as ¬A ∨ ¬B, and ¬(A ∨ B) is the same as ¬A ∧ ¬B. The not moves onto each part, and the operator between them flips.

A truth table proves it by brute force. Two inputs have only four combinations, so trying all of them checks every case there is. The nested loops produce the four rows, and the last column compares the two sides on each row. Every row of both tables says True.

Exam papers usually write the inputs and outputs as 1 and 0, and the operators as NOT, AND and OR or with symbols such as ¬, ∧ and ∨. bit() prints 1 and 0 instead of True and False so that the tables look like the ones you will meet there.

The last line is about precedence. not is worked out before and, so not True and False means (not True) and False, which is False; with the brackets the and is worked out first, and the result is True. When you use De Morgan's laws in code, the brackets are the part that goes wrong.
zh: 德摩根律讲的是 not 作用在一对括号上时会怎样。用考卷上的符号写：¬(A ∧ B) 等于 ¬A ∨ ¬B；¬(A ∨ B) 等于 ¬A ∧ ¬B。not 挪到每一部分上，中间的运算符翻转。
真值表用穷举来证明。两个输入只有四种组合，全试一遍就检查了所有可能的情况。两层循环产生四行，最后一列比较每一行里的两边。两张表的每一行都是 True。
考卷上通常把输入输出写成 1 和 0，运算符写成 NOT、AND、OR，或者 ¬、∧、∨ 这样的符号。bit() 打印 1 和 0 而不是 True 和 False，让这两张表看上去和你在考卷上见到的一样。
最后一行讲的是优先级。not 比 and 先算，所以 not True and False 的意思是 (not True) and False，结果是 False；加上括号，先算 and，结果是 True。在代码里用德摩根律时，出错的往往就是括号。

lineNotes.en: law is whichever function was passed in, first_law or second_law, so one print_table serves both tables.
lineNotes.zh: law 是传进来的那个函数——first_law 或 second_law——所以一个 print_table 能打两张表。

lineNotes.at: print(not True and False, not (True and False))
lineNotes.en: Prints False True: the same three words, grouped differently by the brackets.
lineNotes.zh: 打印 False True：同样三个词，被括号分成了不同的组。

run.expect:
De Morgan's first law
A B | L R | L == R
0 0 | 1 1 | True
0 1 | 1 1 | True
1 0 | 1 1 | True
1 1 | 0 0 | True
De Morgan's second law
A B | L R | L == R
0 0 | 1 1 | True
0 1 | 0 0 | True
1 0 | 0 0 | True
1 1 | 0 0 | True
False True

title.zh: 用 match / case 解析命令

blurb.en: Structural pattern matching reads a short typed command by its shape - how many words, and which word comes first. Needs Python 3.10 or later.
blurb.zh: 结构模式匹配按形状来读一条简短的命令——有几个单词、第一个是什么。需要 Python 3.10 或更高版本。

en: match and case need Python 3.10 or later. On an older Python this program does not run at all - the whole file is rejected with a SyntaxError before the first line executes. If you are not sure what your computer has, run python --version in a terminal (on some computers it is python3 --version).

match takes one value - here the list of words that split() makes from the line - and tries each case from the top. The first pattern that fits runs, and no other case is tried. A list pattern only fits a list of exactly that length: [] fits an empty line, and a two-item pattern never matches three words, which is why take lamp key falls all the way through to the last case.

Inside a pattern a quoted word has to match exactly, while a bare name such as direction or item captures whatever word is in that position. The underscore matches anything and keeps nothing. A vertical bar between two patterns means either one. An if after a pattern is a guard: when it is False the case is skipped and the next case is tried, which is how go up reaches you cannot go that way.

match, case and _ are soft keywords - they are only keywords in this position, so a variable called match elsewhere is still allowed. This is not a switch statement from C or Java: there is no fall-through and no break. Before 3.10 the same job was done with an if / elif chain.
zh: match 与 case 需要 Python 3.10 或更高版本。在更老的 Python 上这个程序根本跑不起来——还没执行第一行，整个文件就以 SyntaxError 被拒绝了。不确定自己电脑上是哪个版本，就在终端里运行 python --version（有些电脑上是 python3 --version）。
match 接收一个值——这里是 split() 从这一行切出来的单词列表——然后从上往下逐个尝试 case。第一个对得上的模式执行，其余的 case 不再尝试。列表模式只对得上长度恰好相同的列表：[] 对得上空行，两项的模式永远对不上三个单词——所以 take lamp key 一路落到了最后一个 case。
模式里加了引号的单词必须一字不差地对上，而像 direction、item 这样的裸名字，会把那个位置上的单词接住。下划线对得上任何东西、但什么都不留。两个模式之间的竖线表示「二者之一」。模式后面的 if 是守卫：它为 False 时这个 case 被跳过、接着试下一个，go up 就是这样走到 you cannot go that way 的。
match、case 和 _ 是软关键字——只在这个位置上才是关键字，所以别处照样可以有一个叫 match 的变量。它也不是 C 或 Java 里的 switch：没有贯穿执行，也没有 break。3.10 之前，同样的事用 if / elif 链来做。

lineNotes.at: case ["go", direction] if direction in DIRECTIONS:
lineNotes.en: A pattern plus a guard: two words, the first exactly go, and the second captured as direction - but only if it is one of the four directions.
lineNotes.zh: 模式加守卫：两个单词，第一个恰好是 go，第二个被接到 direction 里——但只在它是四个方向之一时才算。

lineNotes.en: Any other two-word go command. It must come after the guarded case, or it would catch go north too.
lineNotes.zh: 其余所有两个词的 go 命令。它必须放在带守卫的那个 case 之后，否则会把 go north 也接走。

lineNotes.en: line, not the word list: the message repeats what was typed, spaces and all.
lineNotes.zh: 用的是 line 而不是单词列表：提示里原样重复输入的内容，连空格一起。

run.expect:
'go north' -> you walk north
'go up' -> you cannot go that way
'take lamp' -> you pick up the lamp
'take lamp key' -> unknown command: take lamp key
'' -> nothing typed
'exit' -> goodbye
'dance' -> unknown command: dance
